name: mknod
synopsis: int mknod(const char *pathname, mode_t mode, dev_t dev);
int mknodat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, mode_t mode, dev_t dev);
description: The mknod() system call creates a filesystem node such as a regular file, device special file, or named pipe with the specified mode and device number. It sets the ownership and permissions based on the process's effective IDs and umask. The mknodat() variant allows specifying a directory file descriptor for relative paths.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: The name of the node to create

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Specifies the file type and mode, combined with file mode bits

parameters.name: dev
parameters.description: Specifies major and minor numbers for device special files

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for relative paths (mknodat only)

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The parent directory does not allow write permission, or a directory in the path prefix does not allow search permission
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor (mknodat only)
The user’s quota of disk blocks or inodes on the filesystem has been exhausted
pathname already exists or is a symbolic link
pathname points outside the accessible address space
mode requested creation of an invalid file type
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving pathname
A directory component in pathname does not exist or is a dangling symbolic link
The device containing pathname has no room for the new node
A component used as a directory in pathname is not a directory
mode requested creation of an unauthorized file type and the caller lacks necessary privileges
pathname refers to a file on a read-only filesystem

bugs: There are many infelicities in the protocol underlying NFS that affect mknod() and mknodat().
